races.name: FBC Manby Bowdler Mares' Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning to form with 33 days since last run, suited by the lack of pace pressure
runners_data.spotlight: 1-6 over fences; returned to form of late and although a beaten favourite when runner-up at Fakenham (2m5f, good) last month, that was still a creditable effort; tongue-tie now added; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Charity Barnum
runners_data.note: Hold-up style Irish raider who is a 13-race maiden, needs significant pace collapse to be effective from the rear
runners_data.comment: Irish raider; 13-race maiden who has struggled over fences but the better ground may help.
runners_data.spotlight: Irish raider; 13-race maiden whose best effort came over hurdles when a close second at Tramore (2m5f, good) last August, but three attempts over fences have seen her pulled up twice and tailed off once; Sean Bowen booked and, while a return to better ground and handicap company may help, she still has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Prominent runner trained by in-form Dan Skelton team, 53 days off but should be primed for this assignment
runners_data.comment: Promising hurdler; wind surgery since latest run and respected on chase debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in maiden/novice hurdles before running respectably when third on handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; finished weakly over a slightly longer trip at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) the following month but has since undergone wind surgery; now switches to fences from what looks a workable mark (eased 2lb) and commands respect.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer carrying bottom weight, only 20 days since last run and wearing a hood for the first time
runners_data.comment: Fair third on handicap debut; shaped okay on chase bow; hood is added and now 2lb lower.
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred mare; kept on for a respectable third on handicap hurdle debut at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) last month and shaped reasonably well on chase debut at Stratford (2m1f, good to firm) where she jumped soundly; pedigree suggests this longer trip should suit and a first-time hood may also eke out a little more, now eased 2lb.

races.paceDynamic: She Is For Me Boys will set a steady tempo from the front with no serious early pressure in this small field. Laffer Curve may track prominently but won't force the issue early, while both Charity Barnum and Miss Denver are hold-up performers who will settle at the back. The uncontested lead will allow She Is For Me Boys to dictate terms and control fractions throughout. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners and front-runner, as the lack of pace pressure will suit horses who can travel kindly in the first half of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If She Is For Me Boys gets an easy lead and steady fractions
scenarios.body: The favourite can control the race from pillar to post without being harassed for speed, allowing her recent return to form to translate into victory. Her prominent style is perfectly suited to these tactics with no pace pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get the perfect setup from the slow pace
scenarios.body: Miss Denver or Charity Barnum could benefit from the crawling early pace to unleash a decisive late run. However, they'll need the leaders to come back to them significantly in the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Skelton Tactics Work
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Skelton rides Laffer Curve more aggressively to pressure the leader
scenarios.body: Laffer Curve could force She Is For Me Boys into a genuine pace duel, potentially setting up the race for a closer. The Skelton team's excellent 14-day form suggests tactical awareness.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all runners crawl through the early stages in single file
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure stamina test where the lightweight Miss Denver's late kick could prove decisive. This would require an almost walking pace scenario that seems unlikely given She Is For Me Boys's natural pace.

watchPoints.text: She Is For Me Boys must handle the 33-day break cleanly as any rustiness could undermine her tactical advantage
Watch if Harry Skelton commits to pressuring the leader early on Laffer Curve rather than tracking patiently
Miss Denver's hood first-time could sharpen her significantly for the hold-up role
Charity Barnum needs to jump fluently as an Irish raider with poor fence record facing stronger opposition
Monitor if the genuine good ground suits the prominent runners better than the hold-up horses who may prefer softer

races.name: CopyBet Supporting UK Horse Racing Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Axel Bleue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 17-day break with topspeed headgear, but poor recent handicap form over fences raises questions
runners_data.comment: Point winner; modest since hurdles promise; cheekpieces on but he needs a major step up.
runners_data.spotlight: Point and dual bumper winner in 2025; runner-up in two 2m7f novice hurdles in October but pulled up on handicap debut the following month and has offered little in two runs this spring since a break, including when beaten 24l on last month's chase debut; probably on a workable mark but needs the cheekpieces to have a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rambler
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits, recent winner with strong stamina credentials, but 5lb claiming jockey adds slight uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Improved on reappearance to win at Warwick; up 3lb but F Keighley claims 5lb; big chance.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed the benefit of April's reappearance when back up to a more suitable stamina test off a reduced mark and winning at Warwick (3m, good) the following month; back up 3lb but Freddie Keighley can claim his full allowance; a big player if repeating the effort.

runners_data.name: The Flying Poet
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needs strong pace, recent chase winner but narrow margin suggests limited improvement
runners_data.comment: Scored over hurdles after some near misses then won chase debut; respected off 6lb higher.
runners_data.spotlight: Broke his duck over hurdles after a few near misses and made a winning start to fences at Perth (3m) on his return from a break last month, albeit narrowly with the second making a costly error at the last; lacked fluency there but kept on well and, although a 6lb higher mark asks a question, another bold bid can be expected.

runners_data.name: Hall Lane
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent recent placings, perfectly suited to distance and going conditions
runners_data.comment: 1-13 over fences, but shaping as though his turn in near after three consecutive seconds.
runners_data.spotlight: 1-13 over fences but has been shaping as though his turn is near again after finishing runner-up on his last three starts, all around this trip on good ground when ridden by Jack Hogan; likely to be in the mix again off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Jongleur d'Etoiles
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 85-day break, good hurdles form but still winless over fences in six attempts
runners_data.comment: Multiple hurdle winner; went close over fences at Doncaster latest; contender again.
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple hurdles winner at up to 3m2f, including on a sound surface; 0-6 over fences but went very close at Doncaster (3m2f, good to soft) in March having looked the likely winner; leading contender from an unchanged mark, if repeating that effort.

runners_data.name: Atlanta Brave
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with inconsistent form, 49 days since last run may leave him short of peak fitness
runners_data.comment: No win for three years; third on return but poor since; blinkers on but others preferred.
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't won for three years and struggles for consistency; made an encouraging return when third at Hereford (3m1f, good) in March but couldn't back it up when well beaten at Bangor in refitted cheekpieces last time; blinkers now replace them but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying just 145lbs, recent Fontwell second suggests fencing improvement but still seeking first chase win
runners_data.comment: 0-7 over fences but a close second at Fontwell latest, caught late on; leading player.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 over fences but ran big race in defeat when second at Fontwell (3m2f, good) last month, looking the likely winner until collared on run-in; one of two for the stable and a player off same mark again today.

runners_data.name: Jullou De Grissay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 3lb claiming rider, returning from 51-day break with hurdles win on similar conditions last summer
runners_data.comment: Same mark as hurdle win; chase debut second and wind surgery since; retains potential.
runners_data.spotlight: On the same mark as when winning over hurdles (2m7f, good) last summer, ridden by James King; shaped as though the run was needed in March on return from an absence, before finishing a well-beaten second of three on chase debut the following month; has since undergone wind surgery and retains potential over fences.

runners_data.name: Captain Boudet
runners_data.note: Key pace-setter returning from 81-day break, previous course winner but inconsistent record for new trainer
runners_data.comment: Won at Exeter off 1lb lower but inconsistent since; new stable; visor on; back up in trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 2m3f at Exeter off 1lb lower in March 2025; inconsistent in five starts last season for Jeremy Scott, signing off with a fair second back at Exeter two and a half months ago; has changed hands since and goes back up in trip on stable debut with a visor added; on a good mark if able to put his best foot forward.

runners_data.name: Jack To Bat
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but disappointing in two handicap chase starts, expensive purchase yet to justify price tag
runners_data.comment: £130,000 buy; promising hurdler but disappointing over fences so far; wind surgery since.
runners_data.spotlight: £130,000 buy after runner-up in an Irish point in 2023 and showed promise over hurdles, but his two efforts since switched to fences/handicaps this year have been disappointing; wore this headgear when a remote fourth of four at Wetherby (3m, good to soft) in March and has since undergone wind surgery.

runners_data.name: Est Illic
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying light weight with 7lb claimer, 12-year-old veteran needs to find significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Point winner in April but modest rules form; needs big step up.
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner in April but his rules form is modest; although placed under Jess Stewart on both recent runs in hunter chases, he's been well held; needs to find plenty more back in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Stay Hopeful
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades in finish, poor hurdles form suggests overmatched in this company despite light weight
runners_data.comment: Irish point winner who has yet to show much over hurdles; makes his chase debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner who has yet to show any worthwhile form over hurdles (2m-2m4f) on varying ground, including since switched to handicaps on his last two starts and fitted with cheekpieces; not entirely dismissed on this switch to fences off a basement mark but he needs to step up.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Boudet will control proceedings from the front with his prominent style, likely joined by the other prominent runners Redbridge Rambler, Hall Lane, and Atlanta Brave in the early stages. With only one confirmed front-runner and several prominent types, the pace should be steady rather than breakneck, allowing the field to stay reasonably compact through the middle stages. The hold-up horses The Flying Poet, Jongleur d'Etoiles, Gata Ban, Jack To Bat, and Est Illic will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks over this stamina-testing 2m7f trip. This race shape favors the prominent runners who can track the pace and kick from close range, as the single leader won't be pressured early and the hold-up horses may struggle to make up ground if the pace becomes pedestrian.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Boudet sets a steady pace without serious pressure until the home turn
scenarios.body: The prominent runners tracking behind get first run on the leader and have enough left to repel the late challengers over this demanding trip. Hall Lane, Redbridge Rambler and Axel Bleue are perfectly positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard trying to put Captain Boudet away from the last fence
scenarios.body: The pace becomes strong enough to set up a proper staying test, allowing the hold-up horses with proven stamina to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. The Flying Poet and Gata Ban can capitalize on their patient tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Boudet jumps cleanly and maintains a steady gallop without serious challenge until too late
scenarios.body: The leader's 81-day break proves beneficial as he stays on strongly, with the chasers unable to reel him in over the extended trip. His previous form at similar distances suggests he can see out the trip when allowed an easy lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Boudet sets a crawling pace and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the freshest horses with the best turn of foot prevail regardless of running style. Redbridge Rambler's recent winning form and higher RPR rating give him the edge in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Captain Boudet's jumping under pressure - any mistakes will compromise his front-running tactics and open up the race
The Flying Poet's position turning for home - needs to be close enough to strike as hold-up tactics can backfire over this trip
Hall Lane's response when challenged - has been second in last three starts and needs to show winning mentality
Redbridge Rambler's stamina reserves in final furlong - step up from recent 24f success to this longer trip may stretch him
Jongleur d'Etoiles early in race - 85-day break could leave him needing the run despite previous ability

races.name: Law Without The Horsing Around Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner coming off recent wind surgery success, likely to get uncontested lead but stamina questions over this trip
runners_data.comment: Took advantage of a declining mark to win over fences at Uttoxeter three weeks ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a declining mark to open his account over fences at Uttoxeter (2m5f, good) three weeks ago, on his second start following wind surgery; there should be more to come with that win under his belt and he may well follow up.

runners_data.name: Culligran
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 327-day absence, proven chase winner but stable debut adds uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Won on her second chase start at Newton Abbot last June; absent since last July.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on her second chase start at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last June for John O'Shea; absent since last July and makes stable debut; best watched unless the market speaks in her favour.

runners_data.name: The Moonlight Man
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with poor completion record, pulled up five times from seven starts suggests major reliability concerns
runners_data.comment: Point winner but has been pulled up on five of his seven starts under rules.
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner but has been pulled up on five of his seven starts under rules; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: La Quarite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 270-day break, previous 36-length chase winner but subsequent poor form worrying
runners_data.comment: Won over fences by 36l at Newton Abbot last July; the handicapper in charge since.
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark over fences when scoring by 36l at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last July; the handicapper whacked him up 14lb and after four successive defeats he remains 11lb above his winning mark; must defy a 270-day absence.

runners_data.name: Applicationofcash
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form for new trainer, didn't stay 2m4f last time which raises trip concerns today
runners_data.comment: Responsible for both of his new trainer's wins, the latest at this track 15 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Responsible for both of his new trainer's wins, the latest at this track (2m, good) 15 days ago; didn't appear to see his race out when tried over today's distance at Wincanton in April but he is clearly in good order.

runners_data.name: Pooroldmackley
runners_data.note: Hold-up type switching back to fences after losing hurdle form, 70 days since last run adds to uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Has lost his way over hurdles; hard to fancy on return to chasing
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over fences in April 2025 on heavy, and has won twice over hurdles since but has lost his form in that sphere; now returns to fences; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Majestic Moment
runners_data.note: Strong-finishing hold-up horse in good current form, 3-7 chase record suggests progressive type still improving
runners_data.comment: 3-7 over fences and remains in form following his second at Fontwell 13 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: 3-7 over fences and remains in form following his second at Fontwell (2m3f, good) 13 days ago; may not have finished progressing yet and entitled to be on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Song Of Earth
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose sole chase success came three years ago, 79-day break and age concerns limit appeal
runners_data.comment: Sole success over fences was when trained in Ireland in April 2022; poor since.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success over fences was when trained in Ireland in April 2022; plenty of water under the bridge since and was well below form on all three starts last term; easy to oppose.

runners_data.name: Holy Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist coming off emphatic chase win, 10lb penalty makes task tougher but momentum remains positive
runners_data.comment: Opened his account over fences with an emphatic win at Fontwell last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Opened his account over fences with an emphatic win at Fontwell (2m2f, good) last month; will find it tougher off 10lb higher but should be kept onside.

runners_data.name: Noble Recall
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 253-day absence, satisfactory chase debut but long layoff creates major doubts
runners_data.comment: Made satisfactory chase debut when fourth over C&D last September but has been off since.
runners_data.spotlight: Improved to win off lowly hurdle mark at Southwell (2m4f, good) in May last year; made satisfactory chase debut when fourth over C&D (good) last September but has been off since; this looks a tough assignment on his return.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik will likely lead from the start with no obvious challenger for early pace duties, creating a controlled tempo over this stamina test. The Moonlight Man and La Quarite may sit prominent behind the leader, but the bulk of the field including Majestic Moment, Holy Legend, Culligran, and Applicationofcash will settle further back. This creates a perfect scenario for hold-up horses who can produce late finishing kicks. The lack of genuine pace pressure means front-runners can steal a march, but the 2m4f trip and good ground favor horses with strong finishing speed who can pick up the pieces from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik gets an easy lead with minimal pressure through the early stages
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for closers to make up ground effectively, allowing the front-runner to dictate terms and kick clear when it matters. This tactical advantage proves decisive over the stamina-sapping trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace sets up perfectly for a hold-up horse with genuine finishing kick
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay dividends as the race becomes a sprint from the final fence, with the strongest finisher sweeping past the tiring pace-setters. Class and finishing speed prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If La Quarite or The Moonlight Man can stalk Jiair Madrik and capitalize on any weakening
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get the perfect trip behind the leader and strike when the pace lifts approaching the business end. Their tactical position proves ideal for this intermediate distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Returning Veteran Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Culligran's long absence masks retained ability and the patient hold-up tactics work perfectly
scenarios.body: The 327-day layoff proves beneficial rather than detrimental, with fresh legs and previous course-and-distance success combining for an upset victory. Her proven chase-winning form resurfaces.

watchPoints.text: The Moonlight Man has been pulled up in five of seven starts under rules, making him a serious non-completion risk
Applicationofcash failed to stay 2m4f last time out, so monitor closely for signs of stopping in the final half-mile
Culligran makes stable debut after 327 days off, so watch for market support indicating retained ability
Pooroldmackley has lost all hurdle form recently and switches back to fences after 70-day break
Jiair Madrik sets the pace but question marks exist over his stamina at this extended trip

races.name: Manby Not Mandy Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Delusionofgrandeur
runners_data.comment: Beaten in all six maiden Irish points but in good hands and likely to show improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: 5,700euros foal, 13,000euros 3yo; third foal; dam 2m hurdle winner, half-sister to useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase Golden Hoof; beaten in all six maiden Irish points but in good hands and likely to show improvement under rules.

runners_data.name: Emerald Tir
runners_data.comment: Out of unraced sister to high-class jumper Menorah; may need the run on debut
runners_data.spotlight: £16,000 3yo; sixth foal; dam unraced sister to high-class 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase winner Menorah, out of 2m4f-2m6f hurdle/chase winning half-sister to thorough staying jumper Jet Boys; may need the run on debut.

runners_data.name: Litaque
runners_data.comment: Landed maiden point with the minimum of fuss 15 days ago, and could be hard to beat.
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000euros 3yo, £5,000 Doncaster May 25; eighth foal; half-brother to winners Grozni (bumper and useful 2m4f-4m hurdle/chase) and Donskoye (French 2m6f chase); dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m1f-3m hurdle/chase winner Val De Ferbet; landed maiden point with the minimum of fuss 15 days ago, and could be hard to beat on this rules debut.

runners_data.name: Giant's Way
runners_data.comment: Closely related to high-class 2m hurdler Labaik; yard in decent nick; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: 58,000euros foal, 140,000euros 3yo; eighth foal; closely related to high-class 2m hurdler Labaik, half-brother to winners Danza De La Barre (French 7f-9.5f; RPR 72) and Aiguille Rouge (2m2f hurdle); dam French 5.5f winner (100), out of German 7f Listed winner; yard in decent nick at present and he is one to be interested in; tongue-tie fitted for debut.

runners_data.name: Master Tim
runners_data.comment: Beaten 17l in a point in April; makes rules debut; yard has occasional bumper success.
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam placed in bumpers, sister to point winners Beyondthestorm and Coningbeg, half-sister to 3m1f/3m2f chase winner Kimora, out of unraced sister to bumper winner Culmore Native, half-sister to bumper/2m-2m4f hurdle winner Finns Cross; beaten 17l in a point in April; makes rules debut for yard that has occasional bumper success.

runners_data.name: Storm Dudley
runners_data.comment: Out of a half-sister to a Listed Flat winner but others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam 1m-1m4f maiden (RPR 65), closely related to useful 7f-1m4f winner Cay Dancer, half-sister to 1m2f Listed winner Dynamic, out of French 1m/1m1f winning half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Balisada; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Redbarn
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite in a couple of Irish points; looks likely to show big improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: 50,000euros foal, 30,000euros 3yo, £25,000 Doncaster May 26; fourth foal; dam unraced sister to high-class French staying chaser Rubi Ball; a beaten favourite in a couple of Irish points; she looks likely to show significant improvement in the hands of champion trainer on rules debut.

runners_data.name: Ultimately
runners_data.comment: Beaten 27l on debut over C&D 15 days ago and may do better when he tackles hurdles.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 27l on debut over C&D (good; 80-1) 15 days ago and may do better when he tackles hurdles.

runners_data.name: C'Est Pour Moi
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on debut at Worcester 15 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off on debut at Worcester (2m, good; 8-1) 15 days ago with hood fitted (absent today); likely capable of better but big improvement required.

races.name: #Bepartofit Novices' Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pioneer Pete
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong recent form and 36 days freshening - perfectly positioned to control this weak pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Won Wetherby maiden in March; second in a big-field handicap at Punchestown in May.
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark over hurdles at the fifth attempt in a Wetherby maiden (2m, good) in March; surpassed that with a cracking second in a big-field handicap at Punchestown (2m, yielding) in May and should be up to defying a 7lb penalty in this company.

runners_data.name: Solo Eclipse
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who needs significant pace collapse and hasn't shown progression from promising bumper form to hurdles
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in a bumper at Huntingdon in February but hasn't progressed since.
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising start when runner-up in a bumper at Huntingdon (2m, soft) in February but hasn't progressed on good ground in a similar contest or on hurdles debut at Uttoxeter three weeks ago; may need soft to see him in a better light.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 316-day break with consistent bumper placings but uncertain hurdles ability on debut
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in three bumpers last summer when trained by Ryan Potter.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in three bumpers last summer when trained by Ryan Potter; has changed yards since and best watched on her hurdles debut.

runners_data.name: Fine Fellow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing major improvement from poor Warwick debut but may benefit from handicap-strength field
runners_data.comment: Beaten 26l on hurdles debut at Warwick four weeks ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 26l on hurdles debut at Warwick (2m, good; 25-1) four weeks ago; should do better once he gets a handicap mark.

runners_data.name: Thatsnotmyname
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with modest form who fades in finishes and showed little over this course and distance recently
runners_data.comment: Has shown only modest form in a bumper and on hurdles debut over C&D 15 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown only modest form in a bumper and on hurdles debut over C&D 15 days ago; easy to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Molten Sea
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with proven Flat speed returning from 56-day break after Kempton hurdles success
runners_data.comment: Won on her second hurdles start at Kempton in March; another good run when second since.
runners_data.spotlight: Won three on the Flat for William Haggas; sold for 20,000gns to join this yard last October and scored on her second hurdles start at Kempton (2m good) in March; another good run when runner-up at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) the following month and should run her race.

runners_data.name: Miss Kingston
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with impressive Chepstow win but faces stronger opposition and needs significant pace development
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on her British debut in a Chepstow maiden in April.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 when trained in Ireland; sold for 22,000gns to join current yard in January, and bolted up on her British debut in a Chepstow maiden (2m, good) in April; needs to be taken seriously even with a 7lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Mayo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making hurdles debut after modest bumper form requiring substantial improvement
runners_data.comment: Best effort in third of three bumpers when third at Hereford last month on stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort in third of three bumpers when third of four at Hereford (2m, good to firm) last month on stable debut; hurdles debut and needs to show more.

races.paceDynamic: Pioneer Pete will lead uncontested from the start, setting a comfortable galloping pace with Little Lady Rock and Molten Sea tracking him prominently. The large field of hold-up horses (Solo Eclipse, Fine Fellow, Thatsnotmyname, Miss Kingston, Mayo) will be clustered behind, creating a bunched field turning for home. With no pace pressure on Pioneer Pete and most dangers needing to come from behind, this sets up perfectly for the leaders and prominent racers. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pioneer Pete Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Pioneer Pete jumps cleanly and maintains his lead throughout
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader kicks clear approaching the last hurdle while the pack behind struggles to make up ground on the testing Worcester hill. His superior RPR of 130 and recent Wetherby win prove decisive against horses coming from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Molten Sea or Little Lady Rock apply early pressure to Pioneer Pete
scenarios.body: The pace quickens from halfway as the prominent racers engage, setting up a tactical battle between horses positioned handily. Molten Sea's Flat speed or Little Lady Rock's consistent bumper form prevails in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses and becomes truly crawling
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle, allowing the better-rated closers to unleash their finishing kicks. Miss Kingston's Chepstow maiden win or Pioneer Pete's class edge proves decisive in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Unfancied
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders fail to handle the Good ground or jumping pressure
scenarios.body: The consistent Worcester specialist or improving newcomer capitalizes on market leader errors. Fine Fellow's trainer gets him spot-on for his second hurdles start or Solo Eclipse's bumper form finally translates over timber.

watchPoints.text: Pioneer Pete's jumping accuracy under pressure - any mistake hands initiative to prominent trackers who can capitalize immediately
Little Lady Rock's fitness after 316-day layoff could see her fade if forced to work early against Molten Sea
The pace through the first mile will determine whether hold-up horses like Miss Kingston get their required setup
Molten Sea's stamina beyond her Flat sprinting background if forced into early tactical battle with prominent rivals
Fine Fellow and Solo Eclipse need the pace to completely collapse to have any realistic winning chance from their hold-up styles

races.name: Best Scrap Metal Prices CRS Malvern Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Presenting Milan
runners_data.note: Non-runner, so irrelevant to race dynamics and tactical considerations.
runners_data.comment: Landed Fontwell maiden hurdle in May last year; absent since; handicap debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Won bumper in 2024 and got off the mark on his second outing over hurdles in a Fontwell maiden (2m3f, good; 8-11) in May last year; absent since and makes handicap debut; fascinating contender; market will be best guide.

runners_data.name: Theatre Tom
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 520-day absence, likely needs the run but could benefit from strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in three points and in four novice/maiden hurdles; returns from a lengthy absence.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten in three points and in four novice/maiden hurdles; returns from a lengthy absence and makes handicap debut; likely to need the run; trainer also runs Castle Ivers and Trust House.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to be held up according to spotlight, could be perfectly positioned behind the early pace.
runners_data.comment: Both wins over hurdles have came at Hereford; runner-up at Fontwell last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles have came at Hereford over 2m3f on good; ran up to his best when runner-up at Fontwell (2m3f, good) last month; he needs to be held up to get the best out of him; this is a step up in class and he needs to improve further.

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits tracking the three confirmed front-runners before challenging late in the piece.
runners_data.comment: Completed a double, five months apart, when successful at Bangor in April.
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a double, five months apart, when successful at Bangor (2m7f, good) in April; this is tougher off 7lb higher but may have more to offer in search of a three-timer.

runners_data.name: Castle Ivers
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner stepping up significantly in trip, stamina for 2m4f remains unproven.
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner who made it two out of three over hurdles at Perth when making all.
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner who made it two out of three over hurdles at Perth (2m, good to soft) when making all; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and holds good claims.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner but may need the run after disappointing effort at Warwick following January absence.
runners_data.comment: May have needed the run on first start since January when fourth at Warwick last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Has three wins over hurdles at around 2m; may have needed the run on his first start since January when fourth of eight at Warwick (2m, good) last month and this step up in trip should suit.

runners_data.name: Bertie B
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 411-day break, fresher than most but higher than last winning mark.
runners_data.comment: Has two wins over hurdles but was below his best in his last three starts, in 2025.
runners_data.spotlight: Has two wins over hurdles but was below his best in his last three starts, in 2025, and is still higher than his last winning mark; returns from a 411-day absence and may need to come down in the weights.

runners_data.name: Trust House
runners_data.note: Progressive front-runner with stamina proven, runner-up to stablemate Castle Ivers last time out.
runners_data.comment: Progressive in the spring when winning at Market Rasen and Ffos Las over around 2m.
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in the spring when winning at Market Rasen and Ffos Las over around 2m; no disgrace in finishing runner-up to stablemate Castle Ivers at Perth (2m, good to soft) last time; Sean Bowen prefers Castle Ivers on this occasion but still a contender up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Castle Ivers, Continuance and Trust House will ensure a strong early gallop from the outset, with all three capable of making the running over this extended 2m4f trip. The sustained pace will test stamina reserves through the final half-mile, particularly as Castle Ivers steps up in distance and both Continuance and Trust House look to assert from the front. This searching gallop will favour hold-up horses and those with proven stamina at the trip, as the early leaders may weaken late on. The race shape strongly favours patient, finishing types who can come from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong pace collapses late
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and tie up in the closing stages
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. Oakley and the returning Theatre Tom will benefit most from this searching examination of stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dominates throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Castle Ivers or Trust House gets first run and kicks clear approaching the last
scenarios.body: The winner will have stolen a decisive advantage before the hold-up horses can mount their challenge. Castle Ivers stepping up in trip or Trust House's proven stamina will prove decisive in a tactical masterstroke.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Speed Davis or Oakley travel smoothly in behind the pace-setters throughout
scenarios.body: These horses will be perfectly positioned to strike when the leaders weaken, having saved energy by tracking rather than making the running. Their tactical position will prove superior to both front-runners and hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy scramble finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start with multiple lead changes throughout the race
scenarios.body: The lack of a sustained gallop will favour horses with tactical speed rather than pure stamina, creating an unpredictable finish. Continuance's versatility or Bertie B's fresh legs after a long break could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Castle Ivers and Trust House may go too fast early as stablemates, potentially compromising both chances
Theatre Tom's lengthy absence of 520 days makes fitness a major question mark despite his hold-up style suiting
Continuance needed his last run at Warwick and could strip much fitter for this step back up in trip
Speed Davis carries top weight of 159lbs which may tell in a strongly-run staying test
Oakley has both wins at Hereford over 2m3f on good ground, suggesting these conditions suit perfectly

races.name: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ebony Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 29 days off and yet to win a handicap raises reliability questions
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner (2m-2m5f, good) but yet to win in handicap company and was out of sorts in a light campaign last season; shaped as though the run may have been needed on last month's reappearance but remains with something to prove on recent evidence despite a further ease in the weights.

runners_data.name: The Long Walk
runners_data.note: Solid prominent runner with course form but 61-day break and mixed recent efforts create doubt
runners_data.comment: Runner-up latest and holds solid claims if backing that up with cheekpieces now added.
runners_data.spotlight: Mixed form last season; peak efforts included third at Market Rasen (2m2f) on Boxing Day and second off this mark at Hereford in April latest; not guaranteed to back that up but he's in the mix if repeating that effort with cheekpieces now added.

runners_data.name: Pike Road
runners_data.note: Natural leader gets Keighley's 5lb claim but needs to prove he can lead and deliver off higher mark
runners_data.comment: Dual hurdle winner; form dipped of late but not out of it if improved for comeback run.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2m7f hurdle winner last year, latest success at Uttoxeter (soft) in November off 2lb lower; followed that with a solid effort in a Class 2 at Cheltenham; form has dipped since but recent return may have been needed and he's worth considering with that run behind him.

runners_data.name: Eaton Anne
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace shape, Murphy/Bowen team in good form
runners_data.comment: Reverts to hurdles after going close over fences latest; key player for in-form stable.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who went close to breaking his duck over fences off this mark at Hexham (3m, good to soft) last month, with a tongue-tie added to refitted cheekpieces following a second wind operation; merits serious consideration back over hurdles with the stable in good form.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Strong closer who thrived at Newcastle over similar trip, James Bowen booking catches eye
runners_data.comment: Well held on last month's return; may come on from that but others appeal more.
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner last year; yet to add to that in five hurdle starts but has shown ability, notably when third at Newcastle (2m7f, good) in October; below-par effort in November and well held on last month's reappearance at Perth (3m2f, good to soft); may come on from that but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Balkardy
runners_data.note: Unpredictable but Eleanor Williams' 7lb claim helps, hold-up style suits if he's switched on
runners_data.spotlight: 7-39, with three wins over hurdles, but he's hard to predict and was badly out of sorts in the autumn; unseated early on last month's return and reverts to hurdles off his last winning mark, but it's difficult to know what to expect.

runners_data.name: Impecunious
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner but stable debut suggests needs this run, down in grade helps
runners_data.comment: Should be sharper for last month's return on stable debut and he's worth considering.
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins for Chris Down last year, latest at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) off 3lb lower; well-held fourth of seven on stable/seasonal debut at Worcester (2m5f) but ran well for a long way; worth considering with that run behind him.

runners_data.name: Prince De Juilley
runners_data.note: Classy prominent runner but 215 days off is major concern despite solid autumn form
runners_data.spotlight: Came back to form in the autumn and gained a deserved success at Stratford (2m6f) in October, following that with two solid placed efforts off higher marks, latest at Hereford (3m2f) in November off 2lb lower and all on good ground; has a career-high mark to defy but is reliable and has gone well off a similar break before.

runners_data.name: Gwash
runners_data.note: Struggling to recapture Warwick win form, prominent style less suited to expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Sole win came over two years ago and, though not entirely dismissed, a revival is needed.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to add to his sole win at Warwick (2m3f, good) over two years ago and recent evidence doesn't suggest a breakthrough is imminent; not dismissed completely but needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Peter's Last Deal
runners_data.note: Promising but inconsistent, hold-up style suits but needs to prove he can handle this grade
runners_data.comment: Makes handicap debut; likely capable of better in time but probably best watched for now.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to build on November's promising hurdle debut when third at Hereford (2m3f, good), with progress interrupted by absences and he was always out the back when tailed off on his comeback run 28 days ago; probably capable of better in time but still best watched on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Lacrima
runners_data.note: French chase winner but showing nothing in UK handicap chases, quick return suggests connections keen
runners_data.comment: Switches to hurdles off a lower mark but the step up in trip needs to spark a turnaround.
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick over fences in France last autumn, all around 2m2f on deep ground, but has shown little in three handicap chase runs for this stable this year; reverts to hurdles off a lower mark and the step up in trip needs to spark a turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Pike Road is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate a sustainable tempo from the start without pressure. The prominent racers (Ebony Warrior, The Long Walk, Prince De Juilley, Impecunious, Gwash) will track in behind but none are natural pace-pressers over this trip. This sets up a steady gallop that will gradually intensify from 4f out, with the pace quickening significantly after the second-last hurdle. The lack of early pressure strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay on late, as the moderate early tempo will leave plenty in reserve for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate throughout and quickens late
scenarios.body: Pike Road's lack of pressure creates an ideal scenario for closers who can unleash finishing kicks. Eaton Anne, Fairlawn Skipper and Balkardy benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group maintains position and kicks approaching 2 out
scenarios.body: The Long Walk and Prince De Juilley are best placed to capitalize if they can sustain their effort from ideal tracking positions. Their class tells in a steadily-run contest where positioning matters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pike Road Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Pike Road's sustainable pace proves too economical and he has plenty left
scenarios.body: His dual 2m7f wins show he can dictate and deliver, especially if the chasers leave it too late. Freddie Keighley's 5lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Pike Road struggles or goes too slow and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: A crawling pace becomes a lottery where any horse with a turn of foot can win. Gwash and Prince De Juilley have shown tactical speed in similar scenarios.

watchPoints.text: Pike Road could get an uncontested lead - watch if he builds an early advantage that becomes unassailable
Prince De Juilley's 215-day absence is extreme - monitor early tracking position for signs of ring-rustiness
Balkardy's unpredictable nature means watching his early settling - if he's keen early he won't finish
Eaton Anne's tongue-tie addition last time suggests connections addressing breathing - watch for improved jumping rhythm
The Long Walk needs to track closer than usual after his break - positioning in first mile crucial to chances
